text: Agent existence does not imply agent registration.
Registration does not imply enablement.
Enablement does not imply capability authority.
Capability authority does not imply execution authority.
Tenant scope is an administrative hard boundary.
An agent may not delegate authority it does not possess.
Delegation scope may narrow authority but may not silently widen it.
Revocation must take precedence over previously valid grants for current execution.
Policy version changes must become visible to governed executions according to the active policy contract.
Approval may be granted, revoked, expire, or be superseded independently of agent capability.
A kill switch must override otherwise valid execution permission.
Model/provider admission is administrative policy, not a model choice.
Tool/MCP discovery is not equivalent to tool/MCP admission.
Shared policy reuse must produce consistent administrative decisions across affected agents.
Disabled or retired agents must not execute consequential actions.
Every consequential administrative decision must be attributable to a versioned policy/authority lineage.
Missing audit lineage must never be represented as complete governance evidence.
Successful execution transport is not durable success without authoritative readback where readback is required.
Administrative conflict must not be silently resolved by model preference.
Human or system emergency override must be explicit, attributable, scoped, and separately auditable.
